what: When the footer’s top edge reaches 80% of the screen, a rocket Back to top button rises into the corner from 30px below over .4s power3.out. On hover the nearby star goes out in .2s, the rocket shakes 3px every .02s, and the first flame frame flickers at .7 to 1× scale and .5 to 1 opacity as if starting the engine. On press the page (main) shakes ±10px every .01s and the flame frames cycle every .03s, then .5s later the rocket grows to 2.5× and flies off the top of the screen over 1.5s power4.in while the page follows up to the very top over 1.4s power4.inOut

options.shake: Selector for panels to shake, default main — the original uses main and the info cells in the footer
options.after: Reference element selector for appearing, default nearest footer
options.start: Where it appears (ScrollTrigger start), default top 80%
options.delay: Time from press to rising (s), default .5 — only the screen shakes meanwhile
options.climb: Distance to travel to the top (s), default 1.4
options.[data-fx-part=rocket]: Rocket graphic (inside ship) — shakes on ignition
options.[data-fx-part=fire]: Flame section set (inside ship) — stack several children and they light up in turn. The first section flickers on hover
options.[data-fx-part=stars]: Sparkling star beside it (optional) — it goes out when a hand is placed and falls down and fades away when launched

from.where: shared.js .sg-pagetop (rocket in the chalkboard footer corner) — original Pagetop.astro

note: The button is placed by whichever side uses position: fixed (original 60px from the bottom, inward from the right edge). Scroll to top pushes scrollTop of the window (or the data-fx-scroller plate) with GSAP — if you use a smooth-scroll library, switch to that library’s scrollTo so they don’t collide
